By 1985, the annual take of angel shark on the central California coast had increased to more than 454 tonnes or an estimated 90,000 sharks.

Angiodysplasia.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiodysplasia.question: The _____ was Blood vessel malformation in the gut.
Angiodysplasia.fact: In medicine (gastroenterology), angiodysplasia is a small vascular malformation of the gut.

Angiodysplasia.fact: In this disorder, von Willebrand factor (vWF) is proteolysed due to high shear stress in the highly turbulent blood flow around the aortic valve.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiogenesis.question: The _____ was Blood vessel formation, when new vessels emerge from existing vessels.
Angiogenesis.fact: Angiogenesis is the physiological process through which new blood vessels form from pre-existing vessels, formed in the earlier stage of vasculogenesis. Angiogenesis continues the growth of the vasculature mainly by processes of sprouting and splitting, but processes such as coalescent angiogenesis, vessel elongation and vessel cooption also play a role.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiogenesis.question: Because of this, parenchymal cells will secrete vascular endothelial growth factor (_____-A) which is a proangiogenic growth factor
Angiogenesis.fact: Because of this, parenchymal cells will secrete vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF-A) which is a proangiogenic growth factor.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiogenesis.question: FGF-2 is a more potent angiogenic factor than _____ or PDGF (platelet-derived growth factor); however, it is less potent than FGF-1
Angiogenesis.fact: FGF-1 stimulates the proliferation and differentiation of all cell types necessary for building an arterial vessel, including endothelial cells and smooth muscle cells; this fact distinguishes FGF-1 from other pro-angiogenic growth factors, such as vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), which primarily drives the formation of new capillaries. FGF-2 is a more potent angiogenic factor than VEGF or PDGF (platelet-derived growth factor); however, it is less potent than FGF-1.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiogenesis.question: Mechanically, _____ is upregulated with muscle contractions as a result of increased blood flow to affected areas
Angiogenesis.fact: In vitro studies clearly demonstrate that VEGF is a potent stimulator of angiogenesis because, in the presence of this growth factor, plated endothelial cells will proliferate and migrate, eventually forming tube structures resembling capillaries. VEGF causes a massive signaling cascade in endothelial cells.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiogenesis.question: The increased flow also causes a large increase in the mRNA production of _____ receptors 1 and 2
Angiogenesis.fact: VEGF causes a massive signaling cascade in endothelial cells. Binding to VEGF receptor-2 (VEGFR-2) starts a tyrosine kinase signaling cascade that stimulates the production of factors that variously stimulate vessel permeability (eNOS, producing NO), proliferation/survival (bFGF), migration (ICAMs/VCAMs/MMPs) and finally differentiation into mature blood vessels.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiogenesis.question: Inhibition of _____ prevents the formation of new capillaries
Angiogenesis.fact: MMPs help degrade the proteins that keep the vessel walls solid. Inhibition of MMPs prevents the formation of new capillaries.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiogenesis.question: There have been many studies conducted that have served to determine consequences of the Delta-like _____ 4
Angiogenesis.fact: Dll4 is a transmembrane ligand, for the notch family of receptors. There have been many studies conducted that have served to determine consequences of the Delta-like Ligand 4.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Angiogenesis.question: The _____ pathway is vital to the development of vasculature that in turn, helps the tumors to grow
Angiogenesis.fact: The VEGF pathway is vital to the development of vasculature that in turn, helps the tumors to grow. The combined blockade of VEGF and Dll4 results in the inhibition of tumor progression and angiogenesis throughout the tumor.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Angiogenesis.fact: One of the first applications of pro-angiogenic methods in humans was a German trial using fibroblast growth factor 1 (FGF-1) for the treatment of coronary artery disease.

Angiogenesis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Angiogenesis.fact: Growth factors such as bFGF and VEGF can induce capillary growth into the tumor, which some researchers suspect supply required nutrients, allowing for tumor expansion.

Angiopathy.fact: Angiopathy is the generic term for a disease of the blood vessels (arteries, veins, and capillaries). The best known and most prevalent angiopathy is diabetic angiopathy, a common complication of chronic diabetes.

Angiosperm Phylogeny Group.fact: The Angiosperm Phylogeny Group (APG) is an informal international group of systematic botanists who collaborate to establish a consensus on the taxonomy of flowering plants (angiosperms) that reflects new knowledge about plant relationships discovered through phylogenetic studies.
